paper.title: Expressive Lights for Revealing Mobile Service Robot State
paper.venue: Robot 2015: Second Iberian Robotics Conference, Advances in Intelligent Systems and Computing, volume 417, Springer

relevant_section_or_figure: Sections 3.1–3.2 and Figure 1 define the relevant-state-to-animation mapping: discrete state features select an animation type while continuous parameters modulate it, and the animation persists until a state change. Sections 4.2–4.3 and Algorithm 1 show the small, prioritized vocabulary for waiting, blocked, and progress states.
transferable_principle: Construct a small, legible visual grammar from a selected relevant-state tuple: let discrete, user-important features choose stable visual motifs, and let continuous values modulate those motifs instead of creating a separate visual state for every value or exposing the full internal state.
application_to_world_v21: For the read-only Three.js mirror, select only states a viewer must act on or understand at a glance: worker phase (planning, acting, waiting, blocked, complete), parcel lifecycle, and epistemic status. Give each discrete state one persistent, high-contrast spatial motif attached to the worker or parcel; use fill length, pulse period, trail density, or ring radius for continuous values such as task progress, EON age, or confidence. Keep terrain and geometry in a restrained dark neutral scale so these signals carry hierarchy, and prioritize overlapping states deterministically (for example blocked over working, error over progress). This improves weak scale and unreadable states without copying the paper's light-strip appearance.
falsifier: The principle is falsified for World v21 if first-time viewers, without a legend, cannot reliably distinguish the selected worker/parcel states at overview distance, or if the added motifs increase visual clutter and do not improve state-identification accuracy or response time over the current mirror. It is also falsified if continuous modulation is mistaken for a new discrete state often enough to create operational errors.
fake_evidence: The paper does not study Three.js, SSE, task parcels, EON time, or epistemic states; those are World v21 application concepts, not reported findings.
The paper reports CoBot programmable-light animations and a 38-participant video-based selection study; it does not provide evidence that this exact visual grammar will work in World v21.
No claim is made that the paper's colors, light-strip layout, or specific animations should be copied; only its state-selection and feature/parameter construction is transferred.
